title: WIOD 2014 Analysis
text: region increases final demand, doesn’t just buy local suppliers. imports intermediate inputs regions, turn require inputs suppliers, creating chain reaction. Regional interdependence measures help understand cross-country multiplier linkages. get_regional_interdependence() method computes several key indicators (Miller & Blair, 2009, section 6.3.2): Self-reliance: Average intra-regional column multiplier country (sector-level mean) Total spillover : Block sum foreign output induced unit shocks country Total spillover : Block sum domestic output induced unit shocks abroad Spillover balance: total_spillover_out - total_spillover_in (negative means net recipient cross-region spillovers) Spillover export share: total_spillover_out / (total_spillover_out + total_spillover_in) Now let’s visualize key findings. First, let’s look self-reliance country: plot chunk self_reliance_plot Countries higher self-reliance diversified economies rely less imports intermediate inputs. Next, let’s examine total spillover countries: plot chunk spillover_out_plot Countries higher spillover-tend net importers intermediate inputs, requiring supplies abroad fulfill domestic demand. hand, let’s see countries absorb spillover-effects: plot chunk spillover_in_plot Spillover Balance measures whether specific region sector net “giver” net “receiver” economic stimulus across boundaries: plot chunk spillover_balance_plot balance positive, region net contributor. negative balance indicates country net beneficiary cross-regional spillovers. Finally, let’s examine Spillover Export Share, measures degree external leakages: plot chunk spillover_share_plot higher share indicates larger portion economic stimulus leaks foreign economies. typical highly specialized smaller economies.

title: Friendly Input-Output Analysis
text: Input-output analysis quantitative economic technique examines inter-industry relationships within economy. Developed Russian-American economist Wassily Leontief, models output one industry serves input industries, allowing analysts trace ripple effects changes production, demand, policy throughout economic system. fio package implements input-output analysis using two computational paradigms: Demand-side (Leontief) model: Traces changes final demand propagate backward supply chains, calculating total production required across sectors satisfy given level final demand. Supply-side (Ghosh) model: Traces changes primary inputs propagate forward production chains, analyzing changes value-added components affect sectoral outputs. approaches rely matrix algebra operations implemented Rust computational efficiency, R6 classes providing R user-facing interface.
